history-culture.name: Kigali Genocide Memorial
history-culture.description: A moving memorial and education center commemorating the victims of the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi, with exhibitions that help visitors understand Rwanda's history and path to reconciliation.

history-culture.name: Inema Arts Center
history-culture.description: Contemporary art center showcasing Rwandan artists and promoting cultural exchange through exhibitions, workshops, and studio visits.

history-culture.name: King's Palace Museum
history-culture.description: Historic royal court site where visitors learn about Rwanda's monarchy, traditional architecture, and the ceremonial life of the mwami.

history-culture.name: Ethnographic Museum
history-culture.description: National museum presenting Rwanda's cultural heritage through artifacts, music, crafts, and everyday life across the ages.

history-culture.name: Campaign Against Genocide Museum
history-culture.description: Museum documenting the campaign that stopped the genocide and the rebuilding of national institutions, housed at the Parliament complex.

history-culture.name: Murambi Genocide Memorial
history-culture.description: Powerful memorial site where visitors learn about the genocide through preserved classrooms and curated educational exhibits.

history-culture.name: Presidential Palace Museum
history-culture.description: Former presidential residence turned museum, offering insight into late-20th-century Rwandan political history and daily life of leadership.

history-culture.name: Iby'Iwacu Cultural Village
history-culture.description: Living cultural village where visitors learn traditional Rwandan customs, music, dance, medicine, and community life near Volcanoes National Park.
